title: The App Update
intro: Your bank app says an update is ready. After the last few cases, you are nervous about apps.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: A new version of Orrin is ready

screen.context: The same message also appeared as a banner inside your Orrin app.

msg: Orrin Bank: a new version of the Orrin app is available.

msg.text: Update it from your phone's app store, as usual.
There is no link in this message.
We will never ask you to install an app from a message, or for your PIN or codes.

sender.label: Same thread as your bank texts
sender.lens: It sits with your past messages from the bank.
sender.why: A name proves little. What it asks matters.

store.label: Use your usual app store
store.lens: It tells you to update in the official app store.
store.why: Updating in the official store is exactly right.

nolink.label: No link
nolink.why: No link means nowhere to be tricked.

never.label: Safety reminder
never.lens: It says the bank never asks you to install apps from messages, or for a PIN.
never.why: Real banks warn you about scams.

actions.label: Open my phone's app store and update from there

go_ahead.line: The app store offered the new version of the Orrin app. You updated it there, and nothing else was needed.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real message, and you stayed careful.

block_report.line: That was a real message. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It had no link, told you to use the official store and warned you about scams. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: Update apps in your phone's official app store. A real message never sends you a file or a link to install.

quick_check.q: What made this app update message honest?

options.text: It had no link and told you to update in the official app store

quick_check.explain: No link and the official store are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Same thread as your bank texts
